vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — nineteenth consecutive session since June 27. The July 8 session is defined by the tension between the Chelan Hills Fire's first containment progress and the loss of the atmospheric river's tactical suppression cover for the Sourdough Fire. On the positive side: Chelan Hills moving from 0% to 20% containment with 200+ personnel building line in Douglas County WA is the week's most significant domestic fire management advance. At 9,700+ acres with 100+ structures already destroyed, the fire still represents an extraordinary WUI loss event — but 20% containment in 24 hours, if holding, means initial attack geometry is established and the rate of structural loss is likely stabilized. On the negative side: the atmospheric river window that the Sourdough ICS team was using for initial attack geometry has now closed (July 8 night). The Sourdough Fire (~3,900+ acres as of Day 3) has been burning in steep North Cascades wilderness with aerial-only access; without the AR humidity recovery, conditions revert to the extreme fuel dryness that drove the July 4–5 growth burst. Tomorrow's ICS-209 first containment figure is the operative uncertainty. If any containment percentage appears, the Skagit dam power restoration timeline brightens. If zero containment persists through Day 4 post-AR, the fire is in extended attack at NIFC PL4 Day 10 national resource scarcity — the same constraint that limits what can be redirected from the still-active North Cayuse OR and Crawford Oaks WA fires. On Hormuz: Day 20 of SNSC non-compliance. The Soufan Center's July 7 intelligence brief — the most analytically rigorous read of the Doha talks — assessed that the working groups made 'no headway on nuclear' and that the talks focused on 'issues they said had already been resolved under the MOU.' That framing — avoiding the harder issues to demonstrate procedural progress — is the Doha framework's structural weakness at Day 5 without a compliance declaration. On markets: FOMC minutes are a mild positive — not a clear easing signal, but the 9-9 split and downside labor risk language gives the September cut thesis enough air to survive. Upgrade to Vibe 5 requires: SNSC formal compliance declaration + Sourdough Fire achieving any containment in Day 4 ICS-209 + Skagit dam power restoration signal + Chelan Hills holding 20%+ into Day 5 with no secondary spread. Drop to Vibe 3 requires: SNSC formal re-closure declaration, or Sourdough zero containment through Day 4 and fire-driven merger with any other North Cascades active ignition into a 10,000+ acre complex, or Chelan Hills regression below 20% under post-AR wind event, or Navarre Coulee secondary fire becoming a major fire in its own right at 0% containment.

items.summary: The July 8 geopolitical session enters the twentieth consecutive day without a formal SNSC MOU compliance declaration. The Doha working groups reach Day 5 without their primary deliverable — and the Soufan Center's July 7 intelligence brief, the most analytically grounded read of the Doha round, assessed that the talks made 'no headway on nuclear' and focused on 'issues both sides said had already been resolved under the MOU' — maritime traffic sequencing and frozen fund mechanics — rather than the enrichment and inspection questions that drove the war. This framing is the Doha framework's structural vulnerability: demonstrating working-group procedural activity without advancing the compliance dispute that the SNSC must formally resolve. Iran continues to assert MOU compliance on its own terms while maintaining IRGC 'smart control' over Strait transits — a definitional dispute the US has characterized as MOU-incompatible but has not yet escalated to a formal confrontation. The re-closure is operationally active: tanker traffic at approximately 25 vessels per day against a pre-war average of 110. Lloyd's war-risk normalization remains gated on SNSC declaration and IRGC retraction. The 60-day nuclear window has now consumed one-third of its duration (Day 20 of ~60; window ends approximately August 17) with no formal nuclear talks commenced. No IAEA inspection protocols for bombed sites have been agreed. WTI at Day 12 below the $74 normalization floor — near $69 — remains the commodity market's sustained verdict on deal fragility. Trump's public 'totally unacceptable' rejection of Iran's maximalist peace proposal from July 7 remains the most recent US public diplomatic signal, and the Soufan Center's assessment that 'regime pragmatists have enough political space to translate the MOU into a lasting peace if they can extract sufficient concessions' identifies the working hypothesis for the Doha framework — but Day 20 without a compliance declaration tests that hypothesis.

items.summary: The July 8 session's primary economic event is the 2 PM ET release of FOMC minutes from the June 16-17 meeting — Chair Kevin Warsh's inaugural meeting. The minutes reveal a committee split 9-9 on whether to raise rates in 2026: nine officials projected at least one hike before year-end, eight projected no change, and one projected a cut. Warsh withheld his own rate projection entirely — reinforcing his stated belief that the Fed should respond to data rather than pre-commit to a path — which elevates the minutes themselves to the committee's sole on-record direction signal. Markets read the record as containing downside labor risk acknowledgment: September hike odds per CME FedWatch fell from 66% (pre-minutes) to 50-55% after release. This is not a dovish shift — the 9-9 split is evenly balanced and the hawks are numerically tied with the holds — but the market's reading of downside labor sensitivity in the minutes record is sufficient to sustain the soft-landing rate-cut thesis for September without requiring a clear signal. Warsh's 130-word policy statement from June 17 stripped all forward guidance, meaning today's minutes are the interpretive document the market will use until the next FOMC communication event. On the tariff thread: Section 122 blanket 10% surcharge expires July 24 (T-16). No successor framework has been publicly announced. The most credible successor scenario per trade counsel commentary is USTR's Section 301 investigation (launched March 11), which faces a July 20 completion deadline (T-12) and has a 12.5% duty on 46 countries on the table. Additionally, Pharma Section 232 is scheduled to take effect July 31. The Court of International Trade invalidated Section 122 in May, but the administration has not announced whether it will pursue an expedited appeal or allow the July 24 statutory expiry to render the CIT ruling moot. The tariff succession uncertainty is a material planning obstacle for importers and corporate earnings guidance. SpaceX (SPCX) enters its first full Nasdaq-100 inclusion trading session today (July 8), the day after the effective inclusion date (July 7) triggered mechanical passive fund rebalancing. The market open price relative to SPCX's post-inclusion close will anchor the first full-session narrative for the AI/space infrastructure consolidation from the June 16 ATH ($225.64) to the current ~$162 range.

items.summary: The July 8 infrastructure session is defined by a crucial split in the PNW fire picture: the Chelan Hills Fire achieving its first meaningful containment progress (20%), while the Sourdough Fire's primary tactical resource — the atmospheric river — closes its suppression window tonight, resetting the Sourdough's fire management calculus for extended vs. initial attack tomorrow morning. The Chelan Hills Fire (Day 4, ~9,700+ acres, 20% containment) is the session's primary positive development. At Day 3, the fire stood at zero containment across 9,400-10,000 acres with 0% containment — the Douglas County Fire Marshal's benchmark for the worst structural loss in his 30-year career. By July 8, more than 200 personnel have built sufficient containment line geometry to achieve a 20% containment reading. This is the first indication that initial attack is working in the east-of-Cascades terrain of the Chelan Hills corridor — apple orchard and ranch land between Orondo and Chelan Falls, where dozer access is more feasible than the Sourdough's roadless North Cascades wilderness. A casualty has been confirmed: human remains were found in a burned vehicle within the fire footprint — the first confirmed fatality of the Chelan Hills Fire and the second fatality of the 2026 PNW fire season (after the Upriver Fire in June). A secondary ignition — the Navarre Coulee Fire — has sparked near Lake Chelan, representing a new active fire thread in the same geographic zone as the Chelan Hills Fire. The Navarre Coulee fire's size and containment status are still developing; if it reaches the Chelan Hills Fire footprint under post-AR wind events, it would constitute a new compound ignition event in a critically stressed resource environment. The Sourdough Fire (Day 4, ~3,900+ acres as of last reported ICS-209, Whatcom County WA, North Cascades NP) is approaching its most uncertain tactical moment. The atmospheric river that opened a suppression window July 5-8 has now closed. The AR provided humidity recovery and precipitation benefit to the steep North Cascades terrain — but without fire history data showing actual containment progress during the AR window, it is unknown whether any dozer-impractical aerial-only line geometry was established. SR-20 remains closed indefinitely (Newhalem to Silver Star gate, ~22 miles). Skagit hydroelectric dam power to Seattle (Gorge, Diablo, Ross dams on the Skagit River system) remains disrupted. Tomorrow's Day 4 ICS-209 is the brief's single most important infrastructure data point: any containment percentage post-AR-window means the Sourdough fire management team successfully used the AR window for geometry; zero containment post-AR means the fire is in extended attack at NIFC PL4 Day 10 national aerial resource scarcity. At NIFC PL4 Day 10, Washington remains the primary national draw on aerial suppression resources — Sourdough and Chelan Hills together with Navarre Coulee, while Oregon contributes North Cayuse (east of Pendleton, active behavior, evacuations active) and Crawford Oaks (Dallesport WA Columbia Gorge, structures threatened).

items.summary: Five secondary infrastructure threads entering July 8 evening. First: DOE Energy Emergency Alert for PJM remains nominally active, but the Mid-Atlantic/Northeast heat wave is abating from its July 4-7 peak. Heat indices above 110°F in Philadelphia/DC/NYC have dropped into a more manageable range. Secretary Wright's directive to PJM Interconnections to prevent blackouts remains active. Approximately 779,000 homes without power from severe weather compounding the heat event are working through restoration. Rolling blackout risk is reduced from yesterday's LOCALIZED designation. The heat wave event's most significant infrastructure legacy — beyond the immediate demand spike — is the elevated urgency it provides for the FERC large load integration proceedings: a grid that was demonstrably stretched to emergency thresholds under July 4-7 heat demand is a grid whose large-load integration rules carry high political stakes. Second: FERC AI pathway intervention deadline is TOMORROW COB (T-1). This is the last filing opportunity for any party wishing to participate in the six ISO/RTO show cause proceedings on large-load integration reform. Intervention filings will be the first comprehensive stakeholder map of contested issues. For PNW data center corridors (Quincy WA, The Dalles OR, Eastern Oregon — BPA/WECC jurisdiction), the show cause proceedings are a de facto standard-setter even though BPA/WECC are outside the six ISO/RTO scope. The 30-day informational report deadline (July 20) and 60-day show cause response (August 17) establish the forward calendar for grid reform implementation through summer. Third: NSF Newport, Oregon ocean observatory completed its first major atmospheric river event at Dark Day 10 (removed ~June 28). NWS Portland issued flood watches for SW Washington and NW Oregon during the AR event — without the Newport coastal anchor for flood calibration. This is the first direct confirmation of the monitoring gap's operational consequence: degraded coastal weather calibration at the season's highest-consequence weather event thus far. Senate unanimous reinstallation authorization is in place but physical reinstallation timeline remains pending. Fourth: Longview CSB Day 44. Atmospheric river temperatures provided a brief vapor-pressure risk buffer for the 90,000-gallon hazardous material storage tank through July 8 night. Next elevated risk window: approximately July 11-18 (T-3 to T-10), concurrent with the FERC AI response deadline (July 18), the measles high-consequence sub-window (July 9-12), and the early edge of the estimated next heat event — the three-thread July 11-18 convergence window. Fifth: Washington drought emergency Day 34 (4th consecutive year; 50% snowpack; 12-county emergency declaration). Oregon 83% drought. The AR event is a brief soil moisture injection against a 4-year accumulated deficit — fire fuel conditions remain extreme.

items.summary: The July 8 domestic session adds a new legislative thread to the post-term SCOTUS digestion period: Speaker Johnson, returning from the July 4 recess, has signaled intent to advance the SAVE America Act (voter ID legislation) through a budget reconciliation vehicle (Reconciliation 3.0) — House passed multiple versions but Senate procedural rules ('Byrd bath' requirement that all reconciliation provisions have direct budgetary impact) create significant passage risk. Senate Republicans are openly skeptical that voter ID legislation would survive the Byrd rule review. The OBBB (Day 9) is the active reconciliation vehicle already consuming the Senate's reconciliation bandwidth; a second reconciliation bill in the same Congress would require a new budget resolution. This legislative ambition signals Johnson's post-recess political posture but the procedural pathway is severely constrained. Slaughter (Humphrey's Executor overturned; 6-3) is now in active restructuring phase at FTC, NLRB, SEC, and CFPB — reshaping enforcement posture at agencies regulating financial markets, labor relations, and consumer protection. items.summary: The July 8 PNW session marks the first inflection in the week's most devastating fire event — the Chelan Hills Fire achieving 20% containment after three days at zero — while simultaneously losing the Sourdough Fire's primary suppression resource as the atmospheric river window closes tonight. These developments arrive in compound: the Chelan Hills fire management improvement means line geometry is establishing in the east-of-Cascades WUI terrain; the Sourdough Fire's loss of AR cover means the North Cascades wilderness fire enters its most uncertain 24-hour window of the season, with tomorrow's ICS-209 the definitive indicator of whether initial or extended attack applies at NIFC PL4 Day 10 scarcity. The Chelan Hills Fire (Day 4, ~9,700+ acres, 20% containment) — igniting at 12:05 AM July 4 near US-97 MP-233 between Orondo and Chelan Falls in Douglas County — has progressed from the most devastating WUI structural loss event in Douglas County history (Douglas County Fire Marshal's 30-year benchmark; 100+ structures destroyed; 75% of structures in fire footprint lost; McNeil Canyon devastated) to a fire with initial attack line geometry established. The 200+ personnel building containment lines are working the east-of-Cascades terrain where dozer access is available in a way that the Sourdough's roadless North Cascades wilderness cannot provide. A fatality has been confirmed: human remains found in a burned vehicle within the Chelan Hills fire footprint — the fire's first confirmed death, and the 2026 PNW fire season's second civilian fatality. The Navarre Coulee secondary fire — new ignition near Lake Chelan — introduces a secondary active thread in the same geographic corridor. If Navarre Coulee grows under the post-AR return of summer heat and east wind, it could become an independent structural threat to the Chelan-to-Columbia River corridor. The Sourdough Fire (Day 4, ~3,900+ acres last reported, North Cascades NP/Ross Lake NRA, Whatcom County WA) has lost the atmospheric river's humidity recovery and precipitation benefit that have been its primary aerial suppression resource since July 5. SR-20 remains closed indefinitely (Newhalem to Silver Star gate). Skagit dam power to Seattle (Gorge, Diablo, Ross — Seattle City Light) remains disrupted. The brief's Day 4 ICS-209 watch item is the most consequential fire management data point in the July 8-9 overnight window: any containment percentage means the Sourdough ICS team successfully used the AR window to establish aerial attack geometry; zero containment means the Sourdough is in extended attack classification at NIFC PL4 Day 10 — a nationally constrained resource environment where both Chelan Hills, Navarre Coulee, North Cayuse OR, and Crawford Oaks WA are simultaneously competing for the same aerial tanker and helicopter assets. BPA is managing the post-heat-wave demand reduction with a Skagit hydropower supply reduction still active — the grid transition from heat-wave peak to summer baseline is complicated by the Sourdough Fire's continued proximity to the Skagit dam complex.

analyst_summary: July 8, 2026 evening closes at Vibe 4 — the nineteenth consecutive session at this level since June 27. The session's analytical signature is a controlled pivot: the week's most devastating domestic fire event (Chelan Hills) shows its first containment progress, while the suppression resource enabling that progress (the atmospheric river) simultaneously closes its window for the week's most structurally threatening fire event (Sourdough). These two developments — one positive, one negative — are causally linked: the same AR that enabled Chelan Hills line-building also provided the Sourdough ICS team their suppression window, and both effects expire at the same moment (July 8 night). The resolution of this uncertainty is tomorrow's Day 4 ICS-209 for the Sourdough Fire — the brief's single most consequential data point in the July 8-9 overnight. The FOMC minutes released at 2 PM ET today are the session's most market-significant event. The 9-9 split on 2026 hikes and Warsh's deliberate withholding of his own dot — leaving the minutes as the committee's only on-record direction statement — created a calibrated positive market reading: September hike odds fell from 66% to 50-55%, not because the committee turned dovish, but because the minutes contained enough downside labor risk acknowledgment (in the context of June's 57K NFP miss against a 115K consensus) to keep the September cut thesis alive at even odds. This matters for the PNW specifically: a September cut increases the likelihood that the financial conditions that support PNW data center investment and infrastructure spending continue easing, while a September hike would tighten them and compound the existing wildfire-related economic stress on Douglas County and North Cascades-adjacent economies. On Hormuz: Day 20 without a formal SNSC compliance declaration. The Soufan Center's assessment that the Doha working groups made 'no headway on nuclear' is the most analytically rigorous characterization of where the talks stand after five days of operation. The working groups are functioning as a procedural activity — generating diplomatic contact and demonstrating progress to domestic audiences — without advancing the compliance dispute that the SNSC must formally resolve. The brief's July 11-18 convergence window is now T-3 to T-10: Longview CSB elevated risk, FERC AI 30-day informational report deadline (July 20), and the measles high-consequence sub-window (July 9-12) all land in the same calendar space. Three primary watch items for July 9-10: first, Sourdough Fire Day 4 ICS-209 (July 9 morning) — the atmospheric river's suppression window has now closed; the first containment percentage post-AR determines initial vs. extended attack at PL4 national resource scarcity; Skagit dam power restoration timeline is gated on this figure; second, Measles June 19 high-consequence sub-window opens July 9 — Georgetown University wastewater DNA and ER data fusion surveillance is the primary early-warning mechanism; Day 7 data (July 9) is when Lumen Field community transmission chains would first surface; third, FERC AI pathway intervention deadline COB July 9 — the last filing moment for all six ISO/RTO show cause proceedings; intervention filings will be the first comprehensive stakeholder map of contested issues; PNW data center corridor exposure from Quincy to The Dalles tracks these proceedings as de facto standard-setters.
